items.title: Better gene names, synonyms, and expression data
items.body: A round of nomenclature and data improvements is now live. Every named gene now shows its current dictyBase symbol at the top of its record, and roughly 700 more genes carry their proper name instead of a DDB_G identifier. Old and alternate names are searchable again, so a search for grlL finds far1, and each record now lists these on a Synonyms line under the gene name. Developmental expression now comes from the Rosengarten et al. RNA-seq time course, and the co-expressed gene lists are computed the same way dictyExpress does. Genes affected by the chromosome 2 duplication, such as carA-1 and carA-2, now show the shared expression profile with a note explaining why. In the genome browser, transcripts are labeled by gene name rather than accession. And on each record, the genomic neighborhood view and the genome browser jump now sit together in a new Genome tab.

items.title: Ask AI about a gene or result
items.body: A new Ask AI tool lets you ask a question about a gene, protein, phenotype, or result and get an answer grounded in Dictyostelium biology. Answers are generated by a language model and clearly labeled AI-generated — a starting point to check against the curated records and primary literature, not a substitute for them. Find it under Tools.

items.title: Order strains and plasmids from the Dicty Stock Center
items.body: The Dicty Stock Center is now on the site. Browse the strain and plasmid collections — including the full genome-wide insertion (GWDI) bank — add what you need to a cart, and check out to send your request. Strains default to those currently in stock, and shipping goes on your own FedEx account.

items.title: Contribute annotations with community curation
items.body: You can now add expert, evidence-backed annotations to the genes you know best. A short guided form walks you through the standard curation steps — modeled on PomBase's Canto — and a curator reviews each submission before it goes into the database. Look for "Community Curation" on the homepage.

items.title: BLAST and the genome browser are now live
items.body: The genome tools are fully online: sequence-search any of the 17 hosted dictyostelid genomes with BLAST, explore them in the genome browser, and compare a gene across species. Per-gene sequence downloads, conservation, and natural-variation panels are working too. Thanks for your patience during setup — the site is now feature-complete.

items.title: dictyBase is now live — with one known issue
items.body: dictyBase is now running at dicty.labs.duke.edu. Gene search and records, GO and phenotype enrichment, protein structures, human-disease orthologs, the analysis tools, and the public API are all working. Known issue: BLAST and the other genome-dependent features (per-gene sequence retrieval, the genome browser, and cross-species comparison) are temporarily unavailable while we finish installing the genome databases on the new server — we expect them back shortly. Thanks for your patience, and please send feedback and corrections.

items.title: dictyBase is live in preview
items.body: dictyBase is now hosted at dicty.labs.duke.edu. This is an early preview served from static hosting while the application server is being provisioned, so many interactive features — full gene-record data, BLAST, the analysis tools, and search — are not available yet and will return errors. The site will be fully functional once the backend is in place. Thanks for your patience as we stand it up.

items.title: Quality-of-life upgrades: a tools page, browser jump, and more
items.body: A few smaller improvements. Every gene record now has a 'View in genome browser' button that jumps straight to its locus. A new All tools page collects every analysis tool in one place. Gene Structures tabs show protein stats (length, molecular weight, isoelectric point, hydropathy). And you can now subscribe to site news by RSS.

items.title: Sequence tools: region retrieval, in-silico PCR, and alignment
items.body: A new Sequence tools page pulls genomic DNA by coordinates from any hosted genome, runs in-silico PCR to find a primer pair's amplicons, and builds a multiple sequence alignment of a set of sequences. The genome browser also gains an 'add your own track' option to load your BED, GFF, VCF, or BAM by URL.

items.title: New tools: ID converter, bulk downloads, synteny & variation
items.body: Four additions for working with the data. A gene ID converter maps a mixed list of symbols, DDB_G, UniProt, and NCBI ids into one table. Whole-database TSV downloads (genes, GO, phenotypes, human orthologs) are now on the downloads page. And every gene record's Orthologs tab gains a genomic-neighborhood view that checks whether local gene order is conserved across the dictyostelids, plus a natural-variation panel comparing the protein across the wild D. discoideum isolates.

items.title: New dictyostelid genomes: wild isolates and two more species
items.body: Genome assemblies and annotations from Ahmed et al. 2025 (PNAS) are now on the site. Two new species — D. citrinum and D. dimigraforme — join the comparative tools, and a panel of wild D. discoideum isolates (AX2-214, CR116C, OT3A, M4B, S6B) is now available alongside them. Search any of them with BLAST, view them in the genome browser, or grab the FASTA and annotations on the genome downloads page. Released under CC BY 4.0.

items.title: Annotations now refresh automatically
items.body: Human orthologs, the UniProt accession map, and protein-domain architecture now update each month from UniProt, OMA, and InterPro, so the data stays current without manual rebuilds. Protein domains are precomputed for faster loading on the Structures tab, with a live lookup as a fallback.
